python.work-never-landed/branch:
🚨 unlanded-work-watchdog branch agent/DRE-1-slug: the branch `agent/DRE-1-slug` carries 3 commit(s) that are not on `main`, and no pull request has ever been opened for it — so nothing in the pipeline can see this work. CI, the critic, the merge gate and the Linear sync all key off a pull request; a branch on its own passes through no gate at all and closes no card. Last commit 240 minutes ago.

Where it goes from here: open a pull request from `agent/DRE-1-slug` into `main`. Hand-built work lands exactly the way dispatched work does — the branch, then the pull request, then the same checks and the same critic verdict. What changes is who writes the code, never how it lands.

_Posted once per branch. Opening the pull request ends it._

What is missing, in order: a branch named `agent/DRE-1-<slug>`, then a pull request from it.
